a-loc.summary: Classes and properties for recording where a cultural property is or was located, including addresses, cadastral records, georeferencing, and geological and natural settings.

ac.alt_title_source: file: Core terms defined by Audiovisual Core
ac.summary: Classes and properties for biodiversity media such as images, sound, video, and 3D files, including capture details, regions of interest, and related taxa and specimens.

agls.alt_title_source: file: The AGLS Metadata Terms Namespace provides URIs for the AGLS Metadata Terms Vocabulary.
agls.summary: Classes and properties for describing resources and services to aid discovery, such as the jurisdiction they cover, the laws requiring them, their function, and availability.

agrelon.summary: Classes and properties for relationships between people and organizations, such as kinship, friendship, employment, and correspondence, with the source, reliability, and time span of each.

aiiso.summary: Classes and properties for describing how an academic institution is organized into faculties, schools, departments, and research groups, and the courses and programs they teach.

amo.summary: Classes and properties for describing arguments by their parts, such as claim, evidence, warrant, backing, qualifier, and rebuttal, following the Toulmin model of argument.

aos.summary: Classes and properties for recording a person's sex, gender, and preferences, along with appearance such as skin, eye, and hair color and body measurements.

arch.summary: Classes and properties for describing archival collections, the archives that hold them, their dates, and the people, families, and organizations connected with them.

arco.summary: Classes and properties for concepts used throughout a cultural heritage ontology network, such as parts and wholes, classification, identifiers, agent roles, and locations.

arm.alt_title: Art and Rare Materials (ARM) BIBFRAME Ontology Extensions
arm.alt_title_source: https://art-and-rare-materials-bf-ext.github.io/arm/ (the project's heading). The file's title, "Art and Rare Materials Core Ontology", is left over from version 0.1, whose modules version 1.0 merges.
arm.summary: Classes and properties that extend BIBFRAME for art and rare materials, such as bindings, bookplates, inscriptions, marginalia, watermarks, custodial history, condition, exhibitions, and awards.

as.summary: Classes and properties for describing social activities, such as creating, liking, following, or inviting, and the people, content, and collections involved.

awol.summary: Classes and properties for describing feeds in the Atom syndication format, including their entries, authors, links, categories, and content.

bdo.summary: Classes and properties for describing texts of Asian Buddhist cultures, their versions, volumes, scans, and e-texts, and the people, lineages, and places connected with them.

beijing-palace-lamp-metadata-standards.summary: Classes and properties for describing Beijing Palace lamps, such as their material, patterns, techniques, and uses, and for recording how they were digitized.

bflc.summary: Classes and properties that add library cataloging details to Bibliographic Framework descriptions, such as series treatment, publication statements, encoding level, and authorized access points.

bibframe.summary: Classes and properties for describing works, their instances, and items cataloged by libraries, museums, or archives, along with related agents, subjects, and titles.

bibo.alt_title_source: The file's title, "The Bibliographic Ontology", with its acronym from https://www.dublincore.org/news/2018/11-30-bibo/ (DCMI, its maintainer: "the Bibliographic Ontology (BIBO)").
bibo.summary: Classes and properties for describing documents such as books, articles, theses, letters, legal documents, and web pages, with their authors, identifiers, and citations.

bibtex.summary: Classes and properties for recording BibTeX bibliographic entries, such as articles, books, and theses, with fields including author, title, publisher, and pages.

bio.summary: Classes and properties for describing a person's life as a series of events, such as birth, marriage, employment, and death, and their relationships with others.

bioc.summary: Classes and properties for recording specimens in botanical or zoological collections, such as arboretums, zoos, and herbaria, including their acquisition, provenance, and planting.

biocrm.summary: Classes and properties for describing people and groups, including their roles in events, family, social, and group relationships, occupations, nationalities, gender, and names.

biol.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "Biological Taxonomy Vocabulary 0.2 (Core)", by cutting the version.
biol.summary: Classes and properties for recording the biological classification of plants and animals, from kingdom and phylum through order, family, genus, and species, plus common names.

biro.summary: Classes and properties for describing bibliographic records and references and how they are gathered into reference lists and library catalogs.

bkb.summary: Classes and properties for relating Indonesian cultural heritage to the provinces, regencies, and cities where it originated, developed, was discovered, is located, or is spoken.

blt.summary: Classes and properties that supplement other vocabularies in describing bibliographic resources, such as publication events, Dewey Decimal numbers, and Library of Congress subject headings.

botany.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "Biological Taxonomy Vocabulary 0.2 (Botany)", by cutting the version.
botany.summary: Classes and properties for recording a botanical classification at ranks from domain and kingdom through genus and species down to variety, cultivar, and hybrid.

c4o.summary: Classes and properties for recording how often and where a work is cited, including in-text citations, their surrounding text, and counts from citation services.

cal.alt_title_source: W3C note "RDF Calendar - an application of the Resource Description Framework to iCalendar Data"; the namespace page was not reachable (406).
cal.notes: The live file fails the import check (Turtle parse error); the LOV copy imports. Serve the rescued copy until the live file imports again.
cal.summary: Classes and properties for recording calendar information in the iCalendar format, such as events, to-dos, journal entries, alarms, time zones, and recurrence rules.

cbo.summary: Classes and properties for describing comic books and comic book collections, including issues and series, creators, characters, story content, physical condition, and grading.

cc.alt_title_source: https://www.w3.org/submissions/ccREL/ ("the Creative Commons Rights Expression Language (ccREL)")
cc.summary: Classes and properties for describing copyright licenses, the permissions, requirements, and prohibitions they set for a work, and how to attribute it.

cdesc.summary: Classes and properties for describing the context of a cultural property, such as authorship, dating, acquisition, legal status, inventories, bibliography, documentation, surveys, and conservation work.

cdtype.summary: Classes for identifying the type of a collection description, such as a catalog or index or an analytic, hierarchic, or indexing finding aid.

cerif.alt_title: Common European Research Information Format (CERIF) Ontology
cerif.alt_title_source: file: The Common European Research Information Format (CERIF) Ontology Specification provides basic concepts and properties for describing research information as semantic data.
cerif.summary: Classes and properties for describing research information, such as projects, people, organizations, publications, patents, funding, and equipment, and the dated links between them.

cevent.summary: Classes and properties for describing events involving cultural properties, such as exhibitions and competitions, along with their organizers, awards, and recurrence over time.

cidoc-crm.alt_title_source: file: CIDOC CRM v7.1.3 implemented in RDFS
cidoc-crm.summary: Classes and properties for documenting cultural heritage, including objects, people, groups, places, and the events, such as production and acquisition, that connect them.

cis.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "Cultural-ON (Cultural ONtology): Cultural Institute/Site and Cultural Event Ontology", by cutting the descriptive subtitle.
cis.summary: Classes and properties for describing cultural institutes and sites, such as museums, libraries, archives, and archaeological areas, with their collections, services, and events.

cito.summary: Properties for recording why one work cites another, such as to extend, support, dispute, or use data from it, plus classes for kinds of self-citation.

citof.summary: Classes for grouping citation types from the Citation Typing Ontology by their factual function or their positive, neutral, or negative rhetorical function.

cl.summary: Classes and properties for annotating digital video, including annotation types, relations, time segments, and views for presenting annotations as hypervideos.

cld.summary: Properties for describing collections, such as the types, formats, and creation dates of their items, where they are held, and how they are accessed.

cnt.summary: Classes and properties for recording the content of web pages and other files as text, encoded binary data, or markup, with its character encoding.

co.summary: Classes and properties for grouping resources into collections, sets, and ordered lists, with their members, each item's position and neighbors, and collection size.

country-and-subdivision-representation.summary: Classes and properties for describing countries and their subdivisions, with their letter and numeric codes, English and French names, coordinates, and parent regions.

cpm.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "Catalogus Professorum Model - Version 2.1 (CPM)", by cutting the version.
cpm.summary: Classes and properties for a catalog of university professors, recording their lives, education, careers, offices, memberships, families, pictures, and publications.

crmarchaeo.summary: Classes and properties for documenting archaeological excavation, such as excavation units, stratigraphic layers and their interfaces, embedded objects, and the order of events in time.

crmdig.summary: Classes and properties for documenting digitization and how digital objects are produced and transferred, including the devices and software involved, and for annotations.

crmeh.summary: Classes and properties for recording archaeological excavation and analysis, such as excavation contexts, finds, samples, measurements, drawings, photographs, site divisions, and project teams.

crminf.summary: Classes and properties for recording reasoning in research, such as arguments, beliefs, inferences, the premises and evidence behind them, and provenance assessments.

crmsci.summary: Classes and properties for recording scientific observation, such as sampling, measurements, observed things, and the processes that create or alter physical things.

crmtex.summary: Classes and properties for studying ancient and handwritten texts, such as inscriptions and manuscripts, including their writing, scripts, glyphs, transliteration, and reading.

cro.summary: Classes and properties for describing actions on copyrighted works, such as copying, adapting, translating, performing, broadcasting, and selling, and related agreements and conditions.

ctag.summary: Classes and properties for tagging documents and other resources with keywords linked to concepts, noting whether an author, reader, or tool added each tag.

ctlog.summary: Classes and properties for describing catalog records of Italian cultural heritage, with their versions, identifiers, cataloging agents, access profiles, and privacy levels.

cwork.summary: Classes and properties for describing creative works such as news items, programs, clips, and blog posts, with their titles, thumbnails, audiences, formats, and tags.

cwrc.summary: Classes and properties for describing people's lives, such as their names, family relationships, education, occupations, places, and identities like gender, religion, and class.

cwrc-illness-injury.summary: Classes for categories of illness and injury, such as cancers, infectious diseases, and mental disorders, with properties for their World Health Organization chapters and codes.

daia.summary: Classes and properties for describing the current availability of documents in libraries and similar institutions, including services like loans, their limitations, and expected delays.

dba.summary: Classes and properties for describing historical banking records and the bank activities they document, such as loans, mortgages, guarantees, seizures, and confiscations.

dbpedia-owl.notes: The live file fails the import check (imports nothing); the LOV copy imports. Serve the rescued copy until the live file imports again.
dbpedia-owl.summary: Classes and properties for general subjects across many fields, such as people, places, organizations, buildings, creative works, species, sports, and events.

dc11.alt_title: Dublin Core Metadata Element Set (DCMES), Version 1.1
dc11.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Dublin Core Metadata Element Set, Version 1.1", with its acronym from https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dces/ ("DCMES Version 1.1").
dc11.summary: Fifteen properties for describing any resource, such as its title, creator, subject, description, date, format, language, and rights.

dcat.alt_title_source: The file's title, "The data catalog vocabulary", with its acronym from the file's description.
dcat.summary: Classes and properties for describing data catalogs, the datasets and data services they list, and how each dataset can be accessed or downloaded.

dcite.summary: Classes and properties for describing identifiers and identifier schemes for bibliographic resources such as papers and datasets, and for people, organizations, funders, and licenses.

dcndl.alt_title_source: The name in the publisher's title, which is only in Japanese: RDF Schemaによって定義したNDL Metadata Termsの語彙.
dcndl.summary: Classes and properties for bibliographic and holdings records, such as title and name transcriptions, series, volumes, editions, dissertations, call numbers, and digitization details.

dcterms.notes: The file's own title is "DCMI Metadata Terms - other", naming the terms beyond the fifteen original elements; DCMI calls the whole set "DCMI Metadata Terms".
dcterms.summary: Properties for describing any resource, such as its title, creator, dates, subject, rights, and related resources, plus classes for the kinds of values used.

dctype.summary: Classes for the general type of a resource, such as text, still or moving image, sound, dataset, software, physical object, event, or collection.

ddesc.summary: Classes and properties for the characteristics of cultural property recorded during cataloging, such as measurements, materials, techniques, conservation status, inscriptions, and decoration.

deo.summary: Classes for the rhetorical parts of a document, such as its introduction, methods, results, discussion, acknowledgments, and references.

dicera.summary: Classes and properties for adding metadata to comics, such as issues, story arcs, pages, panels, speech balloons, captions, content ratings, and reading order.

disco.summary: Classes and properties for describing research and survey data for discovery on the Web, such as studies, data files, variables, questionnaires, and statistics.

dm2e.summary: Classes and properties for describing manuscripts and related documents, such as pages, fragments, and posters, with details like opening words, watermarks, shelfmarks, and previous owners.

dnbt.summary: Classes and properties for publication data, such as qualified subjects and languages, canonical and deprecated identifiers, copyright status, and whether an activity was automated.

doap.summary: Classes and properties for describing software projects, such as their releases, source code repositories, licenses, mailing lists, bug trackers, and the people involved.

doco.summary: Classes for the structural parts of a document, such as front matter, chapters, sections, paragraphs, figures, tables, footnotes, and bibliographies.

dpd.summary: Classes and properties for recording when and where a digital picture or document was photographed, developed, digitized, edited, or published, and its location's precision.

dr.summary: Properties linking questions, hypotheses, interpretations, and other resources, such as when one responds to, agrees with, motivates, or is inconsistent with another.

drama.summary: Classes and properties for the elements of drama, such as characters and their goals, plans, beliefs, emotions, and values, and scenes, actions, and conflicts.

dso.summary: Classes and properties for document services like those of libraries, museums, and archives, such as loan, presentation, and open access.

dsw.alt_title_source: Name used by its authors; the namespace page returned 404.
dsw.summary: Classes and properties for connecting organisms, occurrences, events, locations, identifications, taxa, and specimens or other evidence in biodiversity data.

dul.summary: General classes and properties for modeling physical and social entities, such as objects, events, agents, roles, plans, and situations, as a basis for other ontologies.

dwc.alt_title_source: file: Core terms defined by Darwin Core
dwc.summary: Classes and properties for describing organisms, their occurrences, specimens and samples, taxa, identifications, events, locations, geological context, and measurements.

e-collections.summary: Classes and properties for describing collections as structures, such as sets, lists, sequences, and tuples, based on order, uniqueness, element type, and size.

eac-cpf.alt_title: EAC-CPF Descriptions Ontology for Linked Archival Data
eac-cpf.alt_title_source: LOV title without its trailing colon.
eac-cpf.summary: Classes and properties for describing persons, families, and corporate bodies, with names, dates of existence, places, functions, occupations, biographical or historical notes, and relations.

ebucore.summary: Classes and properties for describing audiovisual media, including programs, series, cast and crew, rights, publication events, and the technical formats of audio and video.

eclap.summary: Classes and properties for describing performing arts media, including the professionals involved, performance places and dates, and users' annotations, favorites, and groups.

ecpo.alt_title: Enumeration and Chronology of Periodicals Ontology (ECPO)
ecpo.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Enumeration and Chronology of Periodicals Ontology", with its acronym from http://purl.org/ontology/ecpo (its heading).
ecpo.summary: Classes and properties for recording the volume and issue numbering and dates of a periodical's beginning, ending, and individual issues, including gaps.

ecrm.summary: Classes and properties of CIDOC CRM, implemented in OWL, for documenting cultural heritage objects and related events, people, groups, places, and time spans.

edm.notes: Official file returns 403 to scripted requests; europeana.eu blocks them. Kept in the core; served from the Archivo copy (2024) until Europeana is asked for a fetchable URL.
edm.summary: Classes and properties for aggregating descriptions of cultural heritage objects from many providers, linking objects to their digital representations, agents, places, events, and time spans.

efrbroo.summary: Classes and properties of FRBRoo, implemented in OWL, for describing works, expressions, publications, items, performances, and recordings, and events that create, publish, and reproduce them.

ekc.alt_title: EKC (Encyclopedic Archives of Korean Culture) Data Model vocabulary
ekc.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current title is "EKC Data Model Vocabulary: Ontology Design for the Encyclopedic Archives of Korean Culture (ekc)".
ekc.summary: Classes and properties for modeling Korean cultural heritage, including historical facts, source documents, persons, places, institutions, events, and the relationships among them.

ekcd.summary: Classes and properties for Korean cultural heritage data that record interpretive assertions with their evidence and confidence levels, and utterances such as royal commands.

ep.summary: Classes and properties for describing EPrints repositories, their records, and the documents and files attached to each record.

event.summary: Classes and properties for describing events, such as performances, with their agents, passive factors, products, places, times, and sub-events.

exif.summary: Classes and properties for recording technical data in digital image files, such as camera make and settings, image size and structure, dates taken, and location.

fabio.summary: Classes and properties for describing published and publishable resources, such as books, journal articles, theses, and datasets, as works, expressions, manifestations, and items.

foaf.summary: Classes and properties for describing people, groups, and organizations, their names, online accounts, homepages, images, projects, and the people they know.

fpo.alt_title_source: The file's title, "A Factoid Prosopography Ontology", with its acronym from the file's description.
fpo.summary: Classes and properties for recording what historical sources say about people, such as events, occupations, offices, relationships, possessions, and titles, with citations.

fpr.summary: Properties for linking film works and agents to related cultural heritage objects, such as film copies, trailers, clips, posters, images, texts, and audio.

frad.alt_title_source: Expansion: https://www.iflastandards.info/fr/frad Acronym: the file's title, "FRAD model".
frad.summary: Classes and properties for authority data, describing the names, identifiers, and access points of persons, families, corporate bodies, and works, and how they relate.

frapo.summary: Classes and properties for describing the administration of research projects, such as grant applications, funding bodies, budgets, payments, partners, and project outputs.

frbr.summary: Classes and properties for describing bibliographic works, expressions, manifestations, and items, the people and organizations responsible for them, and relationships such as translation.

frbre.summary: Classes and properties for recording relationships among works, expressions, manifestations, and items, such as parts, adaptations, translations, supplements, summaries, and sequels.

frbrer.alt_title_source: Expansion: https://www.iflastandards.info/fr/frbr/frbrer Acronym: the file's title, "FRBRer model".
frbrer.summary: Classes and properties for describing bibliographic works, expressions, manifestations, and items, with their attributes, relationships, subjects, and the persons and corporate bodies responsible.

frbroo.summary: Classes and properties for describing works, expressions, publications, items, performances, and recordings, the events that create them, and the names and identifiers assigned to them.

frsad.alt_title: Functional Requirements for Subject Authority Data (FRSAD)
frsad.alt_title_source: Expansion: https://www.iflastandards.info/fr/frsad Acronym: the file's title, "FRSAD model".
frsad.summary: Classes and properties for subject authority data, linking subjects to the names used for them, with each name's type, form, language, script, and scheme.

gadm.alt_title_source: The library's name: neither the file nor the publisher names the ontology itself (the publisher's project is GADM-RDF, and the ontology is at http://gadm.geovocab.org/ontology).
gadm.summary: Classes and properties for describing countries and their administrative regions, with names, identifying codes, population, area, and regional or economic classifications.

gamecip.summary: Properties for cataloging video games, such as title, platform, developer, publisher, genre, media format, system requirements, and version.

gen.summary: Classes and properties for linking genealogical data about families, parents and children, spouses, births, deaths, and personal names, and the sources supporting it.

geop.summary: Classes and properties for describing countries, territories, and groups of countries, with their names in several languages, codes, borders, currencies, and statistics such as population.

georss.alt_title_source: file: From the GeoRSS Simple vocabulary
georss.summary: Properties for recording a location as a point, line, polygon, or box, with elevation, floor, and radius.

geosparql.notes: GeoSPARQL 1.1 (modified 2021-10-27), from Archivo's copy of 2024-04-05. OGC's current release, 1.1.1 (2026-02), changes only metadata; its namespace URL serves an annotated summary that imports nothing, and no stable URL serves the file.
geosparql.summary: Classes and properties for representing spatial features and their geometries, with relations such as contains, within, overlaps, and touches, and text encodings of geometries.

gesah.summary: Classes and properties for the inventory, classification, and description of works on paper, such as drawings and prints, with inscriptions, watermarks, collectors' marks, and provenance.

gn.summary: Classes and properties for describing geographical features, especially those in the GeoNames database, with their names, types, coordinates, population, and parent, neighboring, and nearby features.

gndo.summary: Classes and properties for describing persons, families, corporate bodies, conferences, places, works, and subject headings in authority records of the Integrated Authority File.

gov.summary: Classes and properties for describing historical settlements and administrative units, with their names, types, locations, time spans, relationships, and source citations.

graves.summary: Classes and properties for describing human remains, graves, cemeteries, monuments, and memorials, including inscriptions, epitaphs, monument surfaces, locations, and relocations.

gtm.summary: Classes and properties for buildings, streets, plots, and addresses in the city of Gouda over time, and the deeds, permits, and tax records about them.

gvp.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Getty Vocabulary Program ontology", with its acronym from the file's description ("The GVP Ontology").
gvp.notes: The live file fails the import check (Turtle parse error); the LOV copy imports. Serve the rescued copy until the live file imports again.
gvp.summary: Classes and properties for the Getty vocabularies of art and architecture concepts, places, and artists, including hierarchies, preferred terms, biographies, and relationships between entries.

hht.alt_title_source: Expansion and acronym: https://www.irit.fr/recherches/MELODI/ontologies/HHT/index-en.html (heading "Historical Hierarchical Territories: Overview"; "HHT is a modular ontology").
hht.summary: Classes and properties for describing historical territories and their hierarchies as they change over time, including time-bound versions, hierarchy levels, areas, and managing actors.

hico.summary: Classes and properties for recording scholarly interpretations of cultural heritage objects, such as attributions, with their type, supporting criteria, and the sources they come from.

histograph.alt_title_source: Descriptive name: the file has no title and the publisher (histograph.io) is unreachable.
histograph.summary: Classes and properties for relating places in time, such as one place being the same as, lying in, containing, absorbing, or originating from another.

holding.summary: Classes and properties for library holdings that link documents to their copies, copies to agents that hold or collect them, and copies to call numbers.

icon.summary: Classes and properties for recording interpretations of what artworks depict and mean, from recognized motifs and subjects such as characters and symbols to cultural meanings.

iiif-image-2.alt_title_source: IIIF names the specification "IIIF Image API"; this is the 2.x ontology.
iiif-image-2.summary: Classes and properties for describing IIIF images, such as sizes, tiles, scale factors, formats, qualities, and supported features.

iiif-presentation-2.alt_title_source: IIIF names the specification "IIIF Presentation API"; this is the 2.x ontology.
iiif-presentation-2.summary: Classes and properties for arranging an object's pages or views for display, such as manifests, sequences, canvases, ranges, layers, annotation lists, and collections.

immovable-property-arco-network.summary: Classes and properties for describing buildings and other constructions as cultural heritage, including their layout, rooms, floors, roofs, stairs, windows, and technical systems.

information-model-for-visual-arts.summary: Classes and properties for describing visual artworks and how they are made, such as media, materials, techniques, art elements and principles, artists, and collections.

intro.summary: Classes and properties for recording relations between texts and images, such as citation or allusion, and the passages, shared features, and interpretations involved.

isbd.summary: Classes and properties for describing bibliographic resources according to the International Standard Bibliographic Description, such as titles, edition, publication, material description, series, and notes.

isbdu.summary: Properties for recording International Standard Bibliographic Description elements, such as titles, edition, publication, material description, and notes, without limiting them to one class of resource.

iso-thes.summary: Classes and properties for describing ISO 25964 thesauri in SKOS, such as concept groups, compound equivalence, and generic, partitive, and instantial broader and narrower terms.

kanzaki-music.summary: Classes and properties for describing classical music works, performances, and performers, such as symphonies, operas, concerts, venues, composers, conductors, and instrumentalists.

kbv.summary: Classes and properties for library catalog data, such as works, titles, identifiers, carrier types, publication and manufacture, series, shelf marks, and held items.

l4lod.summary: Classes and properties for expressing the licensing terms of linked open data, such as permissions to share, prohibitions on commercial use, and obligations of attribution.

language-representation.summary: Classes and properties for describing languages, language families, dialects, and writing systems, along with language codes such as those in ISO 639.

lawd.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Linking Ancient World Data Ontology", with its acronym from the file's description.
lawd.summary: Classes and properties for describing people, deities, places, names, and written works of the ancient world, and the textual evidence that attests to them.

lcmpt.summary: Properties for authority records of terms for musical instruments and other performing mediums, such as term source, related records, see also references, and time period.

ldr.summary: Classes and properties for expressing rights and licenses for linked data resources, such as reproduction, extraction, and reuse rights, attribution requirements, and access limits.

lexicog.summary: Classes and properties for representing dictionaries and other lexicographic resources as linked data, including their entries, entry structure, and usage examples.

lexinfo.summary: Classes and properties for the linguistic details of lexicon entries, such as part of speech, case, gender, tense, sentence frames, usage notes, and synonyms.

lib.summary: Classes and properties that extend Schema.org for library materials, such as kits, theses, and musical scores, with carriers, place of publication, and holdings counts.

limo.summary: Classes and properties for describing license models for datasets, including the rights, legal terms, and conditions, such as attribution, share alike, and noncommercial use.

lingvo.summary: Classes and properties for describing languages, how well people understand, speak, read, and write them, their official or regional use, and translations.

linked-art.summary: Classes and properties that extend CIDOC CRM for art and cultural heritage, such as payments, transfers, sets and members, custodians, digital services, and rights acquisitions.

lio.summary: Classes and properties for describing what an image shows, such as depicted things, setting, foreground and background, visual parts, technique, materials, and style.

locah.summary: Classes and properties for describing archival collections and their finding aids, including creators, repositories, extent, dates, access restrictions, and custodial history.

locn.summary: Classes and properties for describing any place by its name, address, or geometry, such as street, post code, administrative units, and coordinates.

lode.summary: Classes and properties for describing historical events, including when and where they happened, the agents and things involved, and media that illustrate them.

lom.summary: Classes and properties for describing educational resources with IEEE LOM elements, such as intended users, age range, difficulty, learning time, technical requirements, rights, and classification.

lrmoo.summary: Classes and properties that extend CIDOC CRM for bibliographic information, such as works, expressions, manifestations, items, and the events that create, perform, and reproduce them.

lto.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Library Transaction Ontology", with its acronym from the file's description.
lto.summary: Classes and properties for recording library transactions, such as checkouts, returns, renewals, holds, recalls, interlibrary loans, fines, and patron and item status.

lv.summary: Classes and properties for library catalog data, such as publication types, series and multivolume relations, library and union catalog identifiers, call numbers, and subject headings.

lvont.summary: Classes and properties for describing languages, terms, scripts, and characters, with language codes, translations, and the regions where languages are used.

ma-ont.alt_title_source: The W3C Recommendation's title, "Ontology for Media Resources 1.0" (https://www.w3.org/TR/mediaont-10/), with the version cut.
ma-ont.summary: Classes and properties for describing images and audiovisual media, such as titles, contributors, locations, fragments and tracks, ratings, target audiences, and technical details.

mads.summary: Classes and properties for describing authority data for names, subjects, places, genres, and titles, including their variant forms and relationships to one another.

marc-21-elements-00x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 00X, which hold coded data describing books, maps, music, sound recordings, films, and other materials.

marc-21-elements-0xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 01X to 09X, which hold standard numbers, control numbers, codes, call numbers, and classification numbers.

marc-21-elements-1xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 1XX, which hold the main entry under a personal, corporate, or meeting name or a uniform title.

marc-21-elements-2xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 2XX, which hold titles, edition statements, and details of publication, distribution, and copyright.

marc-21-elements-3xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 3XX, which hold physical description, content and carrier types, and sound, video, and digital file characteristics.

marc-21-elements-4xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 4XX, which hold series statements, including series titles and volume or sequence numbers.

marc-21-elements-5xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 5XX, which hold notes, such as contents, summaries, dissertations, access and use restrictions, and ownership history.

marc-21-elements-60x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 60X, which hold personal names used as subjects.

marc-21-elements-61x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 61X, which hold corporate and meeting names used as subjects.

marc-21-elements-63x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 63X, which hold uniform titles used as subjects.

marc-21-elements-64x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 64X, which hold chronological terms used as subjects.

marc-21-elements-65x.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 65X, which hold topical terms, geographic names, genre or form terms, and other subject and index terms.

marc-21-elements-7xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 7XX, which hold added entries under personal, corporate, and meeting names, titles, and place names.

marc-21-elements-8xx.summary: Properties for the MARC 21 bibliographic fields 8XX, which hold series added entries under personal, corporate, and meeting names and uniform titles.

mdcs.alt_title: Monument Diagnosis and Conservation System (MDCS) damage atlas ontology
mdcs.alt_title_source: file: The Monument Diagnosis and Conservation System (MDCS) damage atlas ontology (MDCS-O) is derived from the original MDCS damage atlas web application
mdcs.summary: Classes for classifying construction damage to monuments and buildings, such as cracking, deformation, biological growth, and surface changes in brick, stone, mortar, plaster, and concrete.

media.summary: Classes and properties for describing media recordings and collections of them, including position in a list, rating, duration, image, sample, and download link.

mediapreserve-required-elements-list.summary: Properties for describing audio, film, and video assets, such as filename, title, date, language, media type, format type, and reel size.

memorix.summary: Classes and properties for records in a collection management system, such as record types, collections, sets, access and rights, change history, and depot locations.

metadata-schema-for-ceramic-resources.summary: Properties for describing ceramic resources, such as patent, report, and standard numbers, series, country, approving body, supervisor, and university.

mmms.summary: Classes and properties for describing manuscripts, such as folio and line counts, decoration, binding, and the people who made, owned, or sold them.

mo.summary: Classes and properties for describing music, including artists and groups, works, performances, recordings, releases and tracks, and media such as vinyl and magnetic tape.

mods-rdf.summary: Classes and properties for describing bibliographic resources, such as titles, names and their roles, subjects, physical form, location and copies, parts, and related items.

movable-property-arco-network.summary: Classes and properties for describing movable cultural property, chiefly specimens such as minerals, rocks, fossils, meteorites, and plant samples, and how they were collected.

mpeg7.alt_title_source: Rhizomik; the namespace page carries no title.
mpeg7.summary: Classes and properties for describing multimedia content, such as audio and video segments, visual and audio features, creation and rights information, and user preferences.

mrel.notes: The live file fails the import check (literal with both a language and a datatype, which EasyRdf rejects); the LOV copy imports. Serve the rescued copy until the live file imports again.
mrel.summary: Properties for stating the relationship between a name and a bibliographic resource, such as author, illustrator, translator, composer, or place of publication.

muninn-military.summary: Classes and properties for describing military people, organizations, and events, such as soldiers, ranks, units, service branches, uniforms, battles, and campaigns.

muninn-organization.summary: Classes and properties for describing people, organizations, and states, and the relationships between them, such as names, roles, ranks, leadership, command, and allegiance.

muo.summary: Classes and properties for describing units of measurement, the physical qualities they measure, and measured values, including base and derived units and prefixes.

mus.summary: Classes and properties for describing musical works, their performances, recordings, and publications, including medium of performance, key, tempo, genre, catalog numbers, and publication statements.

musemeta.summary: Properties for recording museum collection information, such as accessions, loans, exhibitions, condition, storage location, dimensions, creators, and the biological classification of specimens.

muto.alt_title_source: Expansion: file: The Modular and Unified Tagging Ontology (MUTO) is an ontology for tagging and folksonomies. Acronym: the file's title, "MUTO Core Ontology".
muto.summary: Classes and properties for describing how resources are tagged, including who tagged them, private and automatic tagging, tag order, and what each tag means.

national-library-of-scotland-digital.summary: Classes and properties for describing items in a digital object database by title, description, people, places, dates or events, keywords, form or genre, and shelfmark.

naval.summary: Classes and properties for describing ships and their classes, types, hulls, identifying numbers, ports, owners, builders, dimensions, speed, and crew size.

nfo.summary: Classes and properties for describing files, folders, and other desktop resources, such as documents, images, audio, video, software, and archives, and their technical details.

nie.summary: Classes and properties for describing content on a computer desktop and the data objects that store it, such as titles, dates, sizes, languages, and licenses.

nlon.summary: Classes and properties for describing library materials such as books, old books, scores, serials, and online materials, and their authors, subjects, classification numbers, and notes.

nmo.summary: Classes and properties for describing coins, tokens, banknotes, and similar objects, including their mints, issuers, denominations, inscriptions, measurements, wear, and where they were found.

oa.summary: Classes and properties for describing annotations on web resources, including their content, targets, motivations, and the exact part of a resource being annotated.

oad.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Ontology for archival description", with its acronym from the file's description.
oad.summary: Classes and properties for describing archival materials and finding aids, such as levels of description, creators, custody, extent, access conditions, and scope and content.

oc.summary: Classes and properties for describing events within media, the items involved, the timelines they occur on, and how pieces of content relate to each other.

odrl.alt_title_source: Expansion: https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-vocab/ Acronym: the file's title, "ODRL Version 2.2".
odrl.summary: Classes and properties for expressing policies about the use of digital content, such as permissions, prohibitions, duties, constraints, and the parties and assets involved.

odrs.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Open Data Rights Statement Vocabulary", with its acronym from http://schema.theodi.org/odrs/ ("the ODRS vocabulary").
odrs.summary: Classes and properties for recording rights statements for published datasets, such as licenses, copyright and database right holders, and attribution requirements.

og.summary: Properties for describing a web page as an object in a social graph, such as its title, type, image, web address, description, and site name.

oh.summary: Classes and properties for linking something to its opening hours, described with calendars published on the web, and for marking which calendars give closing hours.

olo.summary: Classes and properties for describing ordered lists, including their length, numbered slots, the item in each slot, and the next and previous slots.

om.summary: Classes and properties for describing quantities and measurements in scientific research, including units, prefixes, scales, dimensions, and numerical values.

ontolex.summary: Classes and properties for describing words and multiword expressions, their written and spoken forms and senses, and how they relate to concepts in an ontology.

orca.summary: Classes and properties for recording how certain a piece of information is, the basis on which it is known, and its source.

ore.alt_title: Open Archives Initiative Object Reuse and Exchange (OAI ORE)
ore.alt_title_source: Expansion: http://www.openarchives.org/ore/1.0/vocabulary Acronym: the file's title, "The OAI ORE terms vocabulary".
ore.summary: Classes and properties for describing aggregations, groups of related web resources treated as one, and the resource maps that describe them.

oregon-digital.summary: Properties for recording the contents, contributing institution, conversion specifications, exhibit, and set of items in a digital asset management system.

org.summary: Classes and properties for describing organizations and their structure, including units, sites, posts, memberships and roles, reporting lines, and changes such as mergers.

owl.summary: Classes and properties of the OWL ontology language, for defining kinds of properties, class restrictions, equivalent and disjoint classes, and which individuals are the same.

part.summary: Classes and properties for describing the roles people hold within groups, who holds each role, and the dates they began and stopped performing it.

pav.summary: Properties for recording who authored, curated, or created a digital resource and when, where it was retrieved or imported from, and its earlier versions.

pcdm.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Portland Common Data Model", with its acronym from https://github.com/duraspace/pcdm (the publisher's repository).
pcdm.summary: Classes and properties for organizing digital repository content as collections, objects, and files, and for linking parts to wholes, such as pages to a book.

pcdmuse.alt_title: Portland Common Data Model (PCDM): Use Extension
pcdmuse.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Portland Common Data Model: Use Extension", with its acronym from https://github.com/duraspace/pcdm (the publisher's repository).
pcdmuse.summary: Classes for the role a file plays for the repository object it is attached to, such as original, preservation, service, thumbnail, extracted text, or transcript.

pcdmworks.alt_title: Portland Common Data Model (PCDM): Works Extension
pcdmworks.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Portland Common Data Model: Works Extension", with its acronym from https://github.com/duraspace/pcdm (the publisher's repository).
pcdmworks.summary: Classes for describing works such as books or films, the sets of files that represent them, and their sections, such as chapters or scenes.

pericles-born-digital-archives.alt_title_source: The "Name" on its Ontology Design Patterns page, where the PERICLES project published it: http://web.archive.org/web/2019/http://ontologydesignpatterns.org/wiki/Submissions:Born_Digital_Archives
pericles-born-digital-archives.summary: Classes and properties for describing the units that make up born-digital archives, such as fonds, series, files, and items, how they nest, and their creators.

pericles-computer-system.alt_title_source: The "Name" on its Ontology Design Patterns page, where the PERICLES project published it: http://web.archive.org/web/2019/http://ontologydesignpatterns.org/wiki/Submissions:Computer_System
pericles-computer-system.summary: Classes and properties for describing computers and their hardware, software, operating systems, and drivers, and which components each one uses, requires, or is compatible with.

pericles-digital-video.alt_title_source: The "Name" on its Ontology Design Patterns page, where the PERICLES project published it: http://web.archive.org/web/2019/http://ontologydesignpatterns.org/wiki/Submissions:DigitalVideo
pericles-digital-video.summary: Classes and properties for describing digital video files, such as their containers, codecs, video, audio, and subtitle streams, frame rate, and aspect ratio.

pericles-policy.alt_title_source: The "Name" on its Ontology Design Patterns page, where the PERICLES project published it: http://web.archive.org/web/2019/http://ontologydesignpatterns.org/wiki/Submissions:Policy
pericles-policy.summary: Classes and properties for describing policies, such as their type, statements, version, requirement level, and implementation status, and the processes that implement or validate them.

persee.summary: Classes for types of documents, such as articles, reviews, journal issues, monographs, maps, and parliamentary records, and properties for the dates and places of letters.

person.summary: Classes and properties for describing individual people, such as their birth name, patronymic name, places and countries of birth and death, citizenship, and residency.

place.summary: Classes and properties for describing geographic places, such as countries, counties, towns, rivers, and mountains, which places lie within or overlap others, and their boundaries.

plink.summary: Classes and properties for recording family relationships, such as parents, children, siblings, cousins, in-laws, spouses, and partners, with labels in English, French, and Arabic.

pna.summary: Classes and properties for describing news assets, such as text, images, and video, with their titles, bylines, summaries, dates, embargoes, thumbnails, and transcripts.

pnv.alt_title_source: The file's title, "Person Name Vocabulary", with its acronym from the file's description.
pnv.summary: Classes and properties for recording people's names and their parts, such as given names, surnames and surname prefixes, patronyms, initials, and honorific suffixes.

po.summary: Classes and properties for describing radio and television programs as brands, series, and episodes, with their versions, broadcasts, services, channels, genres, and credits.

premis.summary: Classes and properties for recording metadata that supports the long-term preservation of digital objects, covering events, agents, rights, storage, and integrity checks.

pro.summary: Classes and properties for recording who held a publishing role, such as author, editor, or reviewer, for which document or institution, and when.

prov.summary: Classes and properties for recording the provenance of things: the activities that produced or used them, who was responsible, and what they were derived from.

pso.summary: Classes and properties for recording a document's publishing status over time, such as draft, under review, or published, and the events that change it.

pwo.summary: Classes and properties for describing the steps in publishing a document, such as review and page design, their order, and what each needs and produces.

qudt.alt_title: Quantities, Units, Dimensions and Types (QUDT) Schema
qudt.summary: Classes and properties for describing quantities, units of measure, how to convert between units, dimensions, systems of units, and data types for storing values.

r-arco.summary: Classes and properties for describing cultural property, such as archaeological, artistic, photographic, musical, numismatic, and natural heritage, with categories, components, and catalog numbers.

rcgs.summary: Classes and properties for describing video games, their versions and packages, related materials such as strategy guides and magazines, and game devices and platforms.

rda-c.summary: Classes for the entities work, expression, manifestation, item, agent, collective agent, person, family, corporate body, nomen, place, and timespan.

rda-n.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as the Open Metadata Registry kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rda-n.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of a nomen, such as a name, title, or identifier, including its scheme, language, and script.

rda-onix-framework-element-set.summary: Classes and properties for categorizing the content and carriers of resources by attributes such as sensory mode, image movement, storage medium, and housing format.

rda-p.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as the Open Metadata Registry kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rda-p.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of a place, including its names and its role as a place of birth, publication, or production.

rda-t.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as the Open Metadata Registry kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rda-t.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of a timespan, including its beginning, ending, and role as a date of birth, death, or publication.

rda-w.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rda-w.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of a work, including its creators, subjects, place of origin, and adaptations and other related works.

rda-x.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of an entity of any kind, including its names, identifiers, access points, notes, and related entities.

rdaa.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rdaa.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of persons, families, and corporate bodies, including names, dates, and roles such as composer or editor.

rdae.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rdae.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of an expression of a work, including language, content type, translators, performers, and adaptations.

rdai.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rdai.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of an item, including owners, donors, custodial history, annotators, and restrictions on access and use.

rdam.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rdam.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of a manifestation, including titles, edition, publication details, carrier type, extent, and dimensions.

rdau.alt_title_source: The title of the publisher's earlier file, as LOV kept it; the current file's title drops "RDA".
rdau.summary: Properties for recording the attributes and relationships of all entities without limiting each property to one entity, including titles, contributors, dates, and carrier types.

rdf.summary: Classes and properties of RDF itself, for stating what class a resource belongs to, describing statements, and building lists and containers of items.

rdfs.summary: Classes and properties for describing RDF vocabularies, such as subclasses, subproperties, what a property applies to and takes as values, and labels and comments.

reina-sofia-library-geolocation.summary: Properties for recording where resources are located in the Museo Reina Sofía Library, by type of place, floor, level, and coordinates.

rel.summary: Classes and properties for describing how people are related to or know one another, such as family members, friends, colleagues, employers, mentors, and enemies.

rev.summary: Classes and properties for describing reviews of works, with their reviewer, text, and rating, plus comments on reviews and votes on their usefulness.

rico.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1", by cutting the publisher's name and the version.
rico.summary: Classes and properties for describing archival records and record sets, their carriers, and the people, groups, activities, places, dates, and rules that give them context.

roar.summary: Classes and properties for recording people and places mentioned in archival documents, and for combining several mentions into a single reconstructed person or place.

rov.summary: Classes and properties for describing legally registered organizations, such as companies, with their legal name, company type, status, activity, and registration.

rss.summary: Classes and properties for describing RSS channels: a channel with its title, link, and description, the items it lists, an image, and a text input.

san-lod.summary: Classes and properties for describing archival holdings, the people, families, and organizations that created or keep them, their finding aids, and related places and dates.

saws.summary: Classes and properties for describing medieval manuscript collections of wise sayings, their scribes and editions, and how their texts were copied, translated, and passed on.

schema.summary: Classes and properties for describing things in structured data on web pages, such as creative works, events, organizations, businesses, places, products, and actions.

scholarly-data-model.summary: Properties for describing scholarly works and researchers, such as authors, editors, affiliations, citations, datasets used, the degree of a thesis, and conferences attended.

scoro.summary: Classes and properties for describing the contributions people make and the roles they hold in scholarly research and publications, including the effort involved.

sealit.summary: Classes and properties for describing maritime history: ships and their registration, ownership, construction, and voyages, along with cargo, crews, employment, and wages.

sem.alt_title_source: Name used by its authors; the namespace page was not reachable.
sem.summary: Classes and properties for describing events and the actors, places, and times involved in them, including roles, types, and uncertain time intervals.

shoah.alt_title_source: Not confirmed with the publisher: the file has no title and the publisher's page was unreachable or carries none. Taken from LOV.
shoah.summary: Classes and properties for recording the persecution and deportation of Jews in Italy during the Holocaust: arrests, detention, convoys, camps, liberation, deaths, and family ties.

sioc.alt_title_source: Expansion: file: SIOC (Semantically-Interlinked Online Communities) is an ontology for describing the information in online communities. Acronym: the file's title, "SIOC Core Ontology Namespace".
sioc.summary: Classes and properties for describing online communities such as blogs, message boards, and mailing lists: their sites, forums, user accounts, posts, replies, and topics.

skos.alt_title_source: Expansion: https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/ Acronym: the file's title, "SKOS Vocabulary".
skos.summary: Classes and properties for describing thesauri, classification schemes, subject heading lists, and taxonomies: their concepts, labels, notes, hierarchies, and mappings to other schemes.

skosxl.summary: Classes and properties for treating the labels of concepts in thesauri and similar schemes as resources, so they can be described and linked.

soch.alt_title_source: Swedish National Heritage Board name; the namespace page carries no title.
soch.summary: Classes and properties for describing cultural heritage items from Swedish institutions, with names, materials, inscriptions, measurements, places, periods, images, licenses, and people's roles.

symbolic-music.alt_title_source: Name used by its author; the namespace page returned 403.
symbolic-music.summary: Classes and properties for describing notated music, such as notes, rests, durations, pitches, bars, ties, slurs, voices, and motifs on a score's timeline.

taxon-name-and-rank.summary: Classes and properties for recording names of taxa, such as scientific, common, and synonym names with their authorship, and each taxon's rank and higher groups.

theatre.summary: Classes and properties for describing theater productions, performances, seasons, venues, and the people and companies involved, along with rehearsals, premieres, and accessibility provisions.

thematic-indexes.summary: Properties for describing the thematic indexes of music used in library authority files: composer, full and brief citations, and the abbreviation used in access points.

time.summary: Classes and properties for describing instants and intervals of time, their order and overlap, their durations, and their dates and times in a calendar.

tl.summary: Classes and properties for placing instants and intervals on timelines, such as those behind signals, videos, and scores, and mapping between timelines.

tvc.alt_title: The Time-indexed Value in Context pattern (TVC)
tvc.alt_title_source: The file's title, "The Time-indexed Value in Context pattern", with its acronym from the file's description.
tvc.summary: Classes and properties for recording that someone or something holds a value, such as a role or status, within a time and context.

txn.summary: Classes and properties for describing species concepts, which can carry several names, and linking them to specimens, occurrences, identifications, images, habitats, and web pages.

un.summary: Classes and properties for classifying the uncertainty in a statement by type, nature, whether it is objective or subjective, and the mathematical model used.

unimarc-b-elements-0xx.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 0XX, which hold standard numbers, national bibliography and legal deposit numbers, and other identifiers.

unimarc-b-elements-1xx.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 1XX, which hold coded data on language, country, and characteristics of maps, recordings, films, graphics, and other materials.

unimarc-b-elements-2xx.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 2XX, which hold the title and statement of responsibility, edition, publication details, physical description, and series.

unimarc-b-elements-3xx.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 3XX, which hold notes, such as contents, summaries, dissertations, provenance, awards, and system requirements.

unimarc-b-elements-41x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 41X, which link a resource to its series or subseries and link excerpts or offprints with their sources.

unimarc-b-elements-42x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 42X, which link supplements with their parent resources and link resources issued together or where one updates the other.

unimarc-b-elements-43x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 43X, which link a resource to earlier resources that it continues, supersedes, absorbed, or separated from.

unimarc-b-elements-44x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 44X, which link a resource to later resources that continue, supersede, or absorb it, or that it split into.

unimarc-b-elements-45x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 45X, which link a resource to other editions, translations, and reproductions, or to the original it translates or reproduces.

unimarc-b-elements-46x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 46X, which link a resource to related resources at the set, subset, piece, and piece-analytic levels.

unimarc-b-elements-47x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 47X, which link a review to the item it reviews.

unimarc-b-elements-48x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 48X, which link a resource to others bound in the same volume and to other related works.

unimarc-b-elements-60x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 60X, which hold names, titles, topics, and places used as subjects, and form or genre headings.

unimarc-b-elements-61x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 61X, which hold uncontrolled subject terms, subject categories, and trademarks and hierarchical geographical names used as subjects.

unimarc-b-elements-62x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 62X, which hold the places and dates of publication, performance, and provenance.

unimarc-b-elements-66x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 66X, which hold geographic area codes and time period codes.

unimarc-b-elements-67x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 67X, which hold Universal Decimal Classification and Dewey Decimal Classification numbers and subject index strings.

unimarc-b-elements-68x.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 68X, which hold Library of Congress Classification numbers and class numbers from other schemes.

unimarc-b-elements-7xx.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic fields 7XX, which hold names of persons, corporate bodies, and families responsible for a resource or tied to its ownership.

unimarc-b-elements-801.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 801, which identifies the agencies that created, transcribed, modified, or issued a catalog record, with dates and cataloging rules.

unimarc-b-elements-802.summary: A property for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 802, which holds the code of an International Standard Serial Number center.

unimarc-b-elements-830.summary: A property for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 830, which holds a general note from the cataloger.

unimarc-b-elements-850.summary: A property for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 850, which holds the code of an institution where the resource is held.

unimarc-b-elements-856.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 856, which holds the address, host, access method, and login details for reaching an electronic resource.

unimarc-b-elements-886.summary: Properties for the UNIMARC bibliographic field 886, which holds fields not converted from another record format, with their original tags, indicators, and subfields.

vartrans.summary: Classes and properties for linking entries in a lexicon, and their senses, that are variants or translations of each other, within or across languages.

vcard.summary: Classes and properties for describing people, organizations, groups, and locations with contact details, such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and email, and their relationships.

vgms-expansion-pack-visual-novel.summary: Classes and properties that extend the Video Game Metadata Schema for visual novels, covering gameplay and narrative genres such as dating simulator, noir, and parody.

vgo.summary: Classes and properties for describing video games and their play: genres, players, characters, items, achievements, leaderboards, sessions, and in-game events and purchases.

viaf.summary: Classes and properties for describing name authority records, the clusters that group them, their established and cross-reference headings, and the agencies they come from.

video.summary: Classes and properties for describing videos and films: cast and crew, genres, releases, recording equipment, technical features, scenes, and actions shown on screen.

vir.summary: Properties for recording interpretations of the visual elements in artworks, such as characters portrayed, attributes, personifications, symbolic meanings, and visual prototypes.

vivo.summary: Classes and properties for describing researchers and their positions, organizations, publications, grants, awards, degrees, courses, advising, and presentations.

void.summary: Classes and properties for describing datasets published as linked data: how to access them, their size and subsets, their vocabularies, and links between them.

vra.notes: Published only as RDFa in the HTML page at the namespace. Stored as N-Triples converted from that page, since an HTML file under modules/ would be served as a page on the Omeka site. The GitHub project (mixterj/VRA-RDF-Project) has a converter and samples but no ontology file.
vra.summary: Classes and properties for describing works and images of them, with their creators, dates, places, materials, techniques, measurements, inscriptions, and relations to other works.

wgs84.summary: Classes and properties for recording the latitude, longitude, and altitude of points and other things that have a position.

wittgenstein.alt_title_source: Name used by the Wittgenstein Archives at the University of Bergen; the namespace page returned 404.
wittgenstein.summary: Classes and properties for describing Wittgenstein's manuscripts, typescripts, remarks, letters, and published works, with their parts, dates, and references, and the philosophical subjects they discuss.

wo.summary: Classes and properties for describing species and other taxa, with their names and ranks, habitats, adaptations, behavior, and conservation status.

xtypes.summary: Classes for stating the file format and character encoding of a document at a web address, with properties for file extensions and media types.

zbwext.summary: Classes and properties for describing thesaurus descriptors and folders about persons, companies, subjects, and wares, with document counts, viewer links, and identifiers.

zoology.alt_title_source: file: shortened from its title, "Biological Taxonomy Vocabulary 0.2 (Zoology)", by cutting the version.
zoology.summary: Classes and properties for recording a biological classification, with ranks such as domain, kingdom, genus, species, variety, breed, and strain.
